chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Jafar, from his father, from their ancestors, peace be upon them:

That Ali (peace be upon him) was brought a dispute by a man who had taken a runaway slave who was with him, and then the slave fled from him. Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'He swears by Allah, the One there is no god but He, that he did not strip him of his clothes, nor take anything that was with him or on him, nor sell him, nor be lenient in releasing him. When he has sworn, he is free from liability.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a master who finds a runaway slave he previously owned?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the conditions under which a master is exempt from financial liability (*daman*) for a runaway slave (*abd abiq*) who had previously been in his possession. The exemption is contingent upon the master swearing an oath that he did not strip the slave of his clothes or belongings, sell him, or negotiate his release, thereby ensuring the master's good faith and lack of negligence. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise evidentiary standards and the preservation of property rights within the context of slavery.
